For a math problems, calculus with complex numbers is likely the most complicated that I know I did without help or references.

I built a complete newtonian particle physics simulation. It might have just looked like a bunch of bouncing balls, but those babies were bouncing exactly like how they really would! Very challenging and fun. As for more normal expectations it would undoubtedly be some astronomy for engineers class I took. I didn't really know what to expect, but it turned out to be a full on astrophysics course. Some of the questions and problems were absurdly challenging. Stuff like being given a few bits and pieces of information about a binary star system and then asking for information on another part - perhaps the future orbital trajectory of a body orbiting one of the stars or the mass of one body given information about the characteristics and orbital trajectory of another body in said system. Gets really really funky. On one test a 20% was curved up to a C - I got a 60% on it! Booya! I didn't think too much of it at the time, but I think in hindsight that course actually sparked a serious love for astronomy and astrophysics in me. Awesome professor. A really bizarre feature of the class is that the professor had Tourette's and so in the middle of going over all of this stuff in class he'd occasionally cluck. Good times.
